summary: Windows IPv6 default route persists after docking -> WireGuard tunnel loses internal DNS resolution
summary_short: Docking on Windows causes IPv6 metric to persist; internal DNS routed outside WireGuard
description:
Issue summary:
Several employees with Windows 11 corporate laptops report loss of internal hostname resolution after docking or undocking. Symptoms reproduce when machine switches from Wi‑Fi (802.11) to wired ethernet via a docking station. WireGuard remains connected but traffic to internal .corp hostnames goes to public resolvers (DNS leak) and internal services time out.

Impact:
- Multiple engineers affected intermittently when using docks in office and home setups.
- Affects access to internal services (git, internal dashboards) while the WireGuard tunnel appears UP.
- Increases support overhead; blocks dev workflows and deploys.

Observed behaviour:
- WireGuard interface reports as connected; endpoint reachable for some IP routes.
- ipconfig /all shows an unexpected IPv6 default route assigned to the docked ethernet adapter with lower metric (higher priority) than the WireGuard virtual adapter.
- Windows resolver prefers that interface for AAAA/IPv6 queries; some internal names have AAAA records causing queries to go out to corporate upstream but not through the tunnel.
- Manually changing the interface metric or disabling IPv6 on the physical adapter restores correct routing and internal resolution.

Steps to reproduce (reported):
1) Boot laptop; connect to corporate Wi‑Fi; WireGuard connects and internal hostnames resolve.
2) Dock the machine (ethernet becomes active).
3) Observe that internal names no longer resolve or resolve to external addresses; pings to internal services time out while WireGuard shows active.
4) Run `netsh interface ipv6 show route` and `Get-NetIPInterface` to inspect metrics.

Logs and artifacts attached (representative):
- netsh_ipv6_routes.txt (showing default ::/0 via dock adapter metric 10)
- wg-status.log (WireGuard reports handshake success, latest handshake within interval)
- nslookup_trace.txt (demonstrates queries going to public resolver)

Hypothesis and investigation notes:
- Initial hypothesis: Windows interface metric selection gives the docked ethernet a preferred IPv6 route; WireGuard's virtual adapter has a higher metric so IPv6 traffic bypasses the tunnel.
- Secondary hypothesis: Recent NIC driver update on dock's USB‑Ethernet adapter incorrectly sets interface metrics on link up events, and Windows fails to re-evaluate route priorities for virtual adapters.
- Reproduced on two laptop models (Dell XPS 15, Lenovo T14) running corp image build 2026-01-12. Not reproduced on macOS.
- Temporary mitigation confirms that adjusting interface metrics or disabling IPv6 on physical adapter fixes resolution immediately.

Investigation steps taken so far:
- Collected ipconfig /all and netsh outputs from three affected devices.
- Reproduced in lab with same image and a USB‑C dock: confirmed metric ordering issue.
- Verified WireGuard config (AllowedIPs, Endpoint) is unchanged and includes 0.0.0.0/0 and ::/0 where appropriate.
- Opened vendor support ticket with dock NIC vendor to validate driver behavior.
- SRE ran packet captures showing DNS AAAA queries leaving on ethernet interface.

Temporary workaround provided to users:
- Option A (recommended for quick recovery): Run elevated PowerShell: `Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias \"Ethernet\" -AddressFamily IPv6 -InterfaceMetric 5000` then `ipconfig /flushdns`.
- Option B: Disable IPv6 on the physical ethernet adapter in Network Connections.
- Option C: Unplug dock and reconnect Wi‑Fi (works but disrupts workflow).

Root cause (interim):
"Windows appears to prefer the docked ethernet's IPv6 default route due to a lower interface metric immediately after link-up. A recent USB‑Ethernet adapter driver sets the interface metric aggressively on plug events and Windows does not re-evaluate virtual interface metrics for WireGuard, leading to IPv6 queries bypassing the VPN."

Proposed long-term fixes:
- Change corporate base image to set explicit interface metric policy at provisioning time for virtual adapters (WireGuard) and physical docks.
- Push a small PowerShell startup script to adjust metrics on interface change events until vendor fixes driver.
- Work with driver vendor to correct metric behavior; follow up on vendor ticket.
- Evaluate whether WireGuard Windows client should register a lower metric automatically on tunnel up (coordinate with security/release).

Next actions / owners:
- Diego Morales (Network): finalize PowerShell mitigation and package as signed logon script (ETA 2026-03-16).
- SRE (J. Lin): confirm no packet-level leakage beyond DNS and produce capture summary for security review (ETA 2026-03-15).
- Endpoint team (Maya Singh): test updated driver from vendor and confirm fix before broad rollout.

Resolution: "workaround in place; vendor engaged; ongoing" (will update when vendor provides patched driver).
workaround: Set-NetIPInterface -InterfaceAlias 'Ethernet' -AddressFamily IPv6 -InterfaceMetric 5000 OR disable IPv6 on the physical adapter. Packaged PowerShell script being prepared for deployment.
root_cause: Adapter driver sets low IPv6 interface metric at plug-in and Windows does not adjust WireGuard virtual adapter metric, causing IPv6 DNS queries to prefer the dock adapter and bypass the VPN.
resolution: Pending vendor driver patch. Temporary metric-adjustment script to be rolled out to corp image. No code change to WireGuard required at this time.
